title: indigo_agent_scheduler: add the @hook task header key for hook-only tasks
description:
Problem: a task uploaded to be used as a hook runs at once as an ordinary task when the scheduler is running and has nothing else to do, before the owner can name it in AGENT_SCHEDULER_HOOKS.

Change: a new task header key `// @hook`, without a value, marks a hook-only task.
- A task with `@hook` is never selected as an ordinary task, whether or not AGENT_SCHEDULER_HOOKS names it, exactly like a task named as a hook (`is_hook()` paths in selection, urgent selection, the all-tasks-finished check and the night plan).
- Hooks run it as before when AGENT_SCHEDULER_HOOKS names it.
- AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_STATE shows it with the state `HOOK` and an Idle light. Its priority column shows the assigned hook kind as today (`hook startup` ...). An unassigned one shows `hook`.
- The night plan does not list it, also not as NOT TONIGHT.
- DELETE_ALL keeps it, like the tasks named in AGENT_SCHEDULER_HOOKS.
- The header parser rejects `@hook` with any value and a repeated `@hook`, with a script error message in the style of the other keys.
- An urgent submission with `@hook` is rejected with Alert and a message, because an urgent task cannot be a hook.

Tests: header unit tests (parse, value rejected, repeat rejected) and scheduler integration tests (an `@hook` task uploaded to a running idle scheduler does not start; it runs when then named as a hook; task list label and light; not in the plan; not counted for the automatic stop; DELETE_ALL keeps it; urgent submission rejected).
Docs: the header key table and the Hooks section in indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/doc/SCHEDULER.md, indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (header keys and hooks), and PROPERTIES.md where task labels are described. Bump DRIVER_VERSION (currently 0x03000013).

outcome.summary: 1) indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/indigo_agent_scheduler.c:864: build_task_state_label() still declares 'run_kind kind = hook_kind(device, task);' but no longer uses it after the switch to is_hook(); gcc -Wall reports -Wunused-variable and it costs a redundant hook_kind() lookup. Remove the line. 2) (minor, user-visible wording) indigo_agent_scheduler.c:2595 delete_all_tasks() reports 'tasks named as hooks kept: %d', but the count now includes @hook tasks that no hook names (the new test hook_header_key_task_is_not_planned_or_counted asserts exactly this message for an unnamed @hook task, test_agent_scheduler.c ~line 2291); the comment at line 2571 also still says 'the tasks named as hooks'. Use e.g. 'hook tasks kept' and update the test and comment. Semantics checked with no defect found: is_hook() callers (update_task_states, select_urgent, select_task, all_tasks_finished, estimate message, update_plan, delete_all_tasks, label/light) behave like for named hooks; running-hook detection, chain rule, standby, finish_hook/finish_task and the running-hook plan item use PRIVATE_DATA->kind and name lookup, so they are unaffected; an edit adding/removing @hook on a running task is deferred via pending_text and applied after finish (state set first), on a queued task it takes effect at once like naming/unnaming in HOOKS; RESET/RESET_ALL unchanged; persistence re-parses the text, so @hook survives restore; urgent submission rejected; priority text 'hook' only when no hook names it, per owner note. Docs (SCHEDULER.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md, PROPERTIES.md) consistent; version bumped 0x03000013 -> 0x03000014; formatting OK. Tests: unit hook_key adequate; integration cases hook_header_key_keeps_a_task_from_running, hook_header_key_task_is_not_planned_or_counted, urgent_task_cannot_be_a_hook pass, and all 33 cases matching 'hook' pass locally.

Round 2. Both round-1 findings are fixed: the unused 'kind' in build_task_state_label() is gone (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:863-867 now uses is_hook()), and the DELETE_ALL message reads 'Tasks deleted: %d, hook tasks kept: %d' (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:2590), with the matching tests (test_agent_scheduler.c:2289, 2329, 2341, 2426), the comment (c:2569) and SCHEDULER.md:843. The code is correct: is_hook() includes header.hook and covers selection (c:1607), urgent selection (c:1589), update_task_states (c:1560), all_tasks_finished (c:1663), the plan (c:2234), DELETE_ALL (c:2581), the label and light (c:864-882); task_priority_text gives the hook kind before 'hook'; urgent submission with @hook is rejected (c:2515) and urgent tasks cannot be edited, so @hook cannot reach an urgent task; edits that add or remove @hook go through replace_text (immediately or as a pending edit after a run), and persistence re-parses the stored text, so the flag survives restarts. Parser: no value / repeated key rejected, header memset keeps the default false; KEY_HOOK alignment OK; DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000013 -> 0x03000014; git diff --check clean. Tests: unit hook_key and integration hook_header_key_keeps_a_task_from_running, hook_header_key_task_is_not_planned_or_counted, urgent_task_cannot_be_a_hook, delete_all_keeps_hooks_and_needs_a_stopped_scheduler, delete_all_waits_for_the_shutdown_hook and hooks_run_at_start_idle_and_stop pass. I also checked that a mutant that drops @hook only from select_task fails hook_header_key_keeps_a_task_from_running, so the negative check is effective. REMAINING DEFECT (the same wording issue as in round 1, two places left): indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md:966 says sandbox 'delete_all' deletes 'every task not named as a hook', and the sandbox help in tools/scheduler_sandbox.py:74 says 'delete every task not named as a hook'. Both send DELETE_ALL, which now also keeps unassigned @hook tasks, so both statements are wrong. Fix: change both to 'delete every

Round 3: the three earlier findings are fixed: no unused variable, DELETE_ALL says 'hook tasks kept', and GUIDE:966 and scheduler_sandbox.py:74 now say 'every task that is not a hook task'. No 'every task not named' text is left. I reviewed the whole change. is_hook() now includes header.hook, so selection, urgent selection, update_task_states, all_tasks_finished, update_plan, the estimate message and DELETE_ALL all exclude @hook tasks. hook_kind() is used only in task_priority_text: an assigned kind takes precedence, then 'hook' for an unassigned @hook task, so the label and the Idle light follow the owner's note. The header parser rejects a value ('expected no value') and a repeated key. An urgent @hook submission is rejected with Alert. DRIVER_VERSION goes from 0x03000013 to 0x03000014. Docs are consistent across SCHEDULER.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md and PROPERTIES.md. git diff --check is clean. Tests: the header unit tests cover parsing, a value, a repeat and case. The integration tests cover not starting on an idle running scheduler, running once named, the label and light, the plan, the automatic stop, DELETE_ALL and urgent rejection. Runs: test_agent_scheduler_header passed all cases, and the full test_agent_scheduler run passed 115 of 115 with 0 failed. No defects found.
